The Electronic Communications and Wireless Telegraphy (Amendment and Saving Provision) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations are made in exercise of the power conferred by regulation 5 of the Electronic Communications and Wireless Telegraphy (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (S.I. 2019/246). They replace technical standards referred to in the Commission Delegated Regulation (EU)  305/2013 to include Next Generation (4G/5G) eCall and make provision for existing standards to be saved until 2G networks cease operation.

title: The English Devolution and Community Empowerment Act 2026 (Consequential Amendments) (Precepts) (England) Regulations 2026
summary: The English Devolution and Community Empowerment Act 2026 (c. 23) (“the 2026 Act”) amends the arrangements for the issuing of precepts by mayoral combined authorities and mayoral combined county authorities. Section 12 of the 2026 Act removes the restriction under which precepts may be issued only in respect of mayoral functions.

title: The Over the Counter Derivatives (Intragroup Transactions) Regulations 2026
summary: Regulation (EU) No  648/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 4 July 2012 on OTC derivatives, central counterparties and trade repositories (EUR 2012/648) (“the EMIR Regulation”) sets out obligations for over-the-counter (OTC) derivatives contracts to be cleared through central counterparties, establishes risk management requirements for uncleared derivatives contracts and provides for exemptions in relation to certain intragroup transactions. Further temporary provisions were made in relation to these exemptions in Part 5 of the Over the Counter Derivatives, Central Counterparties and Trade Repositories (Amendment, etc., and Transitional Provision) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 (S.I. 2019/335) (“the 2019 Regulations“).

title: The Overseas Prudential Requirements Regime (Credit Institutions and Investment Firms) Regulations 2026
summary: Section 1 of, and Schedule 1 to, the Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 (c. 29) revoke Regulation (EU) No.  575/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 June 2013 on prudential requirements for credit institutions and investment firms and amending Regulation (EU) No  648/2012 (“the Capital Requirements Regulation”). Articles 81(1)(a)(iii), 82(a)(iii), 107(4), 114(7), 115(4) and 116(5) of the Capital Requirements Regulation enable the Treasury to determine that a third country applies prudential and supervisory requirements equivalent to those applied in the United Kingdom in relation to credit institutions and other types of firms. The revocation of articles 81(1)(a)(iii), 82(a)(iii), 107(4), 114(7), 115(4) and 116(5) comes into force on 1st January 2027 by virtue of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 (Commencement No. 15 and Saving and Transitional Provisions) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/682 (C. 56)).

title: The Power to Award Degrees etc. (MLA College Ltd) Order 2026
summary: This Order authorises MLA College Ltd (UKRPN: 10049370) to grant taught awards up to and including master’s level for subjects related to engineering and technology, business and management, and geography, earth and environmental studies, including but not limited to the subjects specified in the Schedule. The authorisation is for a fixed term beginning on 25th October 2026 and expiring at the end of the day on 24th October 2030.

The Intimate Image Reports (Trusted Flagger) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations designate South West Grid for Learning Trust (“the Trust”) as a suitable person to make intimate image reports to providers of internet services and providers of internet access services. The Trust operates a service called the Revenge Porn Helpline which will receive information from the public and make the reports, the purpose of which is to assist providers in making judgments about whether content is intimate image content, as defined in section 59(10A) of the Online Safety Act 2023 (c. 50).

The Levelling-up and Regeneration Act 2023 (Commencement No. 12) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations are the twelfth commencement regulations under the Levelling-up and Regeneration Act 2023 (c. 55) (“the 2023 Act”). They bring section 232 of the 2023 Act (“section 232”) into force. Section 232 amends sections 72A, 107A and 107B of the Marine and Coastal Access Act 2009 (c. 23) (“the 2009 Act”) to confer power on the Secretary of State and the Scottish Ministers, in respect of cases where they are the appropriate licensing authority, to make regulations to charge fees for the monitoring of a marine licence and the variation and transfer of a marine licence. It also amends sections 98, 108 and 110A of the 2009 Act in connection with those new powers. Section 232(9) revokes the Public Bodies (Marine Management Organisation) (Fees) (Order) 2014 (S.I. 2014/2555).
